11: # FreeLLMAPI
12: 
13: **One OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Sixteen free LLM providers. ~1.7B tokens per month.**
14: 
15: Aggregate the free tiers from Google, Groq, Cerebras, NVIDIA, Mistral, OpenRouter, GitHub Models, Cohere, Cloudflare, HuggingFace, Z.ai (Zhipu), Ollama, Kilo, Pollinations, LLM7, OVH AI Endpoints, and OpenCode Zen — plus custom OpenAI-compatible chat, embedding, image, and audio endpoints — behind a single `/v1` API. Keys are stored encrypted. A router picks the best available model for each request, falls over to the next provider when one is rate-limited, and tracks per-key usage so you stay under every free-tier cap.

50: ## Why this exists
51: 
52: Every serious AI lab now offers a free tier — a few million tokens a month, a few thousand requests a day. On its own each tier is a toy. Stacked together, they add up to roughly **1.7 billion tokens per month** of working inference capacity, across 100+ models from small-and-fast to reasonably capable.
53: 
54: The problem is that stacking them by hand is painful: seventeen different SDKs, seventeen different rate limits, seventeen places a request can fail. FreeLLMAPI collapses that into one OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Point any OpenAI client library at your local server, and it routes transparently across whichever providers you've added keys for.

93: ## Features
94: 
95: - **OpenAI-compatible** — `POST /v1/chat/completions` and `GET /v1/models` work with the official OpenAI SDKs and any OpenAI-compatible client (LangChain, LlamaIndex, Continue, Hermes, etc.). Just change `base_url`.
96: - **Responses API** — `POST /v1/responses` (the wire format current Codex CLI versions require) is implemented as a translating shim over the same router, with full streaming events and tool calls.
97: - **Editor autocomplete** — `POST /v1/completions` translates legacy prompt/suffix requests into the same router, so VS Code ghost-text clients such as Continue can use FreeLLMAPI for inline suggestions.
98: - **Anthropic Messages API** — `POST /v1/messages` (plus `/v1/messages/count_tokens`) speaks Anthropic's wire format over the same router, so **Claude Code** and the official Anthropic SDKs run against your free pool. `GET /v1/models` is content-negotiated (Anthropic shape when the client sends `anthropic-version`, OpenAI shape otherwise), and Claude families (`opus` / `sonnet` / `haiku` / `default`) map to `auto` or a pinned model on the Keys page. See [Anthropic / Claude clients](#anthropic--claude-clients).
99: - **Image generation & text-to-speech** — `POST /v1/images/generations` and `POST /v1/audio/speech` route across the providers that serve media models, including custom OpenAI-compatible media endpoints. Browse and toggle them on the dashboard's **Models → Image / Audio** tabs.
100: - **Streaming and non-streaming** — Server-Sent Events for `stream: true`, JSON response otherwise. Every provider adapter implements both.
101: - **Tool calling** — OpenAI-style `tools` / `tool_choice` requests are passed through, and assistant `tool_calls` + `tool` role follow-up messages round-trip across providers.
102: - **Embeddings** — `/v1/embeddings` with family-based routing, including custom OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoints: failover only ever happens between providers serving the *same* model (vectors from different models are incompatible), never across models. See [Embeddings](#embeddings).
103: - **Automatic fallover** — If the chosen provider returns a 429, 5xx, or times out, the router skips it, puts the key on a short cooldown, and retries on the next model in your fallback chain (up to 20 attempts).
104: - **Per-key rate tracking** — RPM, RPD, TPM, and TPD counters per `(platform, model, key)` so the router always picks a key that's under its caps.
105: - **Sticky sessions** — Multi-turn conversations keep talking to the same model for 30 minutes to avoid the hallucination spike that comes from mid-conversation model switches.
106: - **Encrypted key storage** — API keys are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before hitting SQLite; decryption happens in-memory just before a request.
107: - **Unified API key** — Clients authenticate to your proxy with a single `freellmapi-…` bearer token. You never expose upstream provider keys to your apps.
108: - **Dashboard login** — The admin UI and all `/api/*` routes are gated behind an email + password account (scrypt-hashed, session-token auth), set on first run. The `/v1` proxy keeps its own unified-key auth for apps.
109: - **Health checks** — Periodic probes mark keys as `healthy`, `rate_limited`, `invalid`, or `error` so the router skips dead ones automatically.
110: - **Admin dashboard** — React + Vite UI to manage keys, reorder the fallback chain, inspect analytics, and run prompts in a playground. Dark mode included.
111: - **Analytics** — Per-request logging with latency, token counts, success rate, and per-provider breakdowns.
112: - **Context handoff on model switch** — Optional. When a session falls over to a different model, injects one compact system message so the new model knows it is continuing an existing task. Disabled by default; enable with `FREELLMAPI_CONTEXT_HANDOFF=on_model_switch`. See [Context Handoff](#context-handoff).
113: - **Runs anywhere Node 20+ runs** — Windows, macOS, Linux servers, or a small ARM SBC (Raspberry Pi included). ~40 MB RSS at idle behind PM2 / systemd / whatever supervisor you prefer.
114: 
115: ## Not yet supported
116: 
117: The scope is deliberately narrow. If a feature isn't on this list and isn't below, assume it isn't there yet.
118: 
119: - **Moderation** (`/v1/moderations`)
120: - **`n > 1`** (multiple completions per request)
121: - **Per-user billing / multi-tenant auth** — single-user by design
122: 
123: PRs that add any of these are very welcome. See [Contributing](#contributing).
124: 
125: ## Quick start
126: 
127: **One-liner** (Docker required — sets up `~/freellmapi`, generates an encryption key, pulls the image, and starts the container):
128: 
129: ```bash
130: curl -fsSL https://freellmapi.co/install.sh | bash
131: ```
132: 
133: Prefer to read before you pipe to bash? [The script is here](https://freellmapi.co/install.sh). Re-running it is safe: your `.env` (and encryption key) is preserved and the container updates to `:latest`. Override the defaults with `FREELLMAPI_DIR`, `PORT`, or `HOST_BIND` env vars.
134: 
135: On Windows, the easiest path is the desktop **[`.exe` installer from Releases](https://github.com/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi/releases/latest)** (below); the Docker steps work in WSL or any bash shell.
136: 
137: **Or manually with Docker Compose.** It runs the API and dashboard together on port 3001 and persists SQLite in a named volume.
138: 
139: **Prerequisites:** Docker, Docker Compose, OpenSSL.
140: 
141: ```bash
142: git clone https://github.com/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi.git
143: cd freellmapi
144: 
145: # Generate an encryption key for at-rest key storage
146: ENCRYPTION_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
147: printf "ENCRYPTION_KEY=%s\nPORT=3001\n" "$ENCRYPTION_KEY" > .env
148: 
149: docker compose up -d
150: ```
151: 
152: Open http://localhost:3001, add your provider keys on the **Keys** page, reorder the **Fallback Chain** to taste, and grab your unified API key from the **Keys** page header. That unified key is what you point your OpenAI SDK at.
153: 
154: > **Reaching it from another machine?** By default the container is published only on `127.0.0.1`, so `http://<server-ip>:3001` won't load from another device (the page just hangs). To expose it on your LAN — e.g. a Raspberry Pi at `http://192.168.1.x:3001` — start it with `HOST_BIND=0.0.0.0`:
155: >
156: > ```bash
157: > HOST_BIND=0.0.0.0 docker compose up -d
158: > ```
159: >
160: > Only do this on a trusted network: the proxy is single-user and guarded only by the unified API key.
161: 
162: ### Local development
163: 
164: **Prerequisites:** Node.js 20+, npm.
165: 
166: ```bash
167: git clone https://github.com/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi.git
168: cd freellmapi
169: npm install
170: cp .env.example .env
171: ENCRYPTION_KEY="$(node -e 'console.log(require("crypto").randomBytes(32).toString("hex"))')"
172: printf "ENCRYPTION_KEY=%s\nPORT=3001\n" "$ENCRYPTION_KEY" > .env
173: npm run dev
174: ```
175: 
176: `ENCRYPTION_KEY` is required for startup. The server only falls back to a
177: database-stored development key when `DEV_MODE=true` and `NODE_ENV` is not
178: `production`; do not use that fallback with real provider keys.
179: 
180: Request analytics are retained for 90 days or 100000 request rows by default,
181: whichever limit prunes first. Set `REQUEST_ANALYTICS_RETENTION_DAYS=0` or
182: `REQUEST_ANALYTICS_MAX_ROWS=0` in `.env` to disable either retention limit.
183: 
184: Open http://localhost:5173 (the Vite dev UI), add your provider keys on the **Keys** page, reorder the **Fallback Chain** to taste, and grab your unified API key from the **Keys** page header. That unified key is what you point your OpenAI SDK at.
185: 
186: ### Declarative startup config
187: 
188: For repeatable Docker/server installs, FreeLLMAPI can apply a JSON config on
189: every boot. Set `FREEAPI_CONFIG_PATH=/path/to/freellmapi.config.json` or put the
190: same JSON in `FREEAPI_CONFIG_JSON`. The config is idempotent: existing keys,
191: custom providers, model edits, fallback rows, and routing settings are updated
192: instead of duplicated.
193: 
194: ```json
195: {
196:   "keys": [
197:     { "platform": "groq", "key": "gsk_...", "label": "main" },
198:     { "platform": "google", "key": "AIza...", "enabled": true }
199:   ],
200:   "customProviders": [
201:     {
202:       "baseUrl": "http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1",
203:       "label": "Ollama",
204:       "models": [
205:         { "model": "llama3.1:8b", "displayName": "Local Llama", "supportsTools": true }
206:       ]
207:     }
208:   ],
209:   "models": [
210:     {
211:       "platform": "groq",
212:       "modelId": "llama-3.3-70b-versatile",
213:       "displayName": "Llama 3.3 70B",
214:       "supportsTools": true,
215:       "fallbackEnabled": true
216:     }
217:   ],
218:   "routing": { "strategy": "balanced" }
219: }
220: ```
221: 
222: > **Reaching the dev UI from another device on your LAN?** Use `npm run dev:lan` — it passes `--host` through to Vite, which then prints a `Network: http://<your-ip>:5173` URL you can open from a phone or another machine. (Plain `npm run dev -- --host` does *not* work here: the root `dev` script is a `concurrently` wrapper, so the flag never reaches Vite.) API calls go through Vite's dev proxy, so no extra server config is needed.
223: 
224: For a production build without Docker:
225: 
226: ```bash
227: npm run build
228: node server/dist/index.js     # server + dashboard both served on :3001
229: ```
230: 
231: ## Docker
232: 
233: FreeLLMAPI publishes a single production image that contains the Express server and the built React dashboard:
234: 
235: ```bash
236: docker pull ghcr.io/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi:latest   # or pin a release, e.g. :v1.2.3
237: ```
238: 
239: The image is multi-arch (`linux/amd64` + `linux/arm64`, so it runs on a Raspberry Pi). Published tags: `latest` (default branch), `v*.*.*` (git release tags), and `sha-<commit>`.
240: 
241: The included `docker-compose.yml` is the recommended install path:
242: 
243: ```bash
244: docker compose up -d
245: docker compose logs -f freellmapi
246: ```
247: 
248: By default the container's port is bound to `127.0.0.1` (localhost only). To reach the dashboard/API from another machine on your network, publish it on all interfaces with `HOST_BIND=0.0.0.0 docker compose up -d` — only on a trusted LAN, since the proxy is single-user.
249: 
250: SQLite data is stored in the `freellmapi-data` volume at `/app/server/data`.
251: Keep the same `.env` `ENCRYPTION_KEY` and volume when upgrading, because
252: provider keys are encrypted at rest. If your host only persists a specific
253: directory, set `FREEAPI_DB_PATH=/that/path/freellmapi.db`.
254: 
255: On hosts with ephemeral disks, configure an encrypted backup target:
256: 
257: ```env
258: FREEAPI_DB_BACKUP_PATH=/app/server/data/freellmapi.db.backup
259: # or:
260: FREEAPI_DB_BACKUP_URL=https://example.com/freellmapi.db.backup
261: FREEAPI_DB_BACKUP_TOKEN=optional-bearer-token
262: FREEAPI_DB_BACKUP_KEY=64-char-hex-backup-key
263: FREEAPI_DB_BACKUP_INTERVAL_MS=300000
264: ```
265: 
266: When the database file is missing at startup, FreeLLMAPI restores the backup
267: before migrations run. While the server is running it uploads a fresh encrypted
268: backup periodically. If `FREEAPI_DB_BACKUP_KEY` is omitted, the app uses
269: `ENCRYPTION_KEY` for the backup envelope too.
270: 
271: More Docker operations and examples live in [docker/README.md](./docker/README.md).
272:
